concept: Progress shows how far a device task has run, like a washer's cycle or a firmware update, as a recessed groove in the body that fills with printing ink, with its name and reading printed above, and it never moves while idle.

default_to_avoid.pattern: thin Material linear progress bar in the brand colour with a looping indeterminate stripe
default_to_avoid.why_not: The brand colour spends the unit's one orange on a reading, and a stripe that loops for ever is idle motion that P6 forbids.

default_to_avoid.pattern: progress bar with a percentage floating inside the fill
default_to_avoid.why_not: Text over a moving fill changes contrast as it passes, and P5 wants labels printed on the inset line instead.

references.source: Braun SK 4 radio-phonograph (Dieter Rams, Hans Gugelot, 1956): a long recessed tuning scale along the front of the case
Braun T 1000 world receiver (Dieter Rams, 1963): a linear scale window read from left to right
system/refs/ref-01.png: fader groove with a ruler scale beside the display (estimated from chat)

derivation.consequence: a level that fills a groove is a part, the ring tone lit along its upper edge, never screen ink
derivation.form: The fill is line.ring, the resin tone that keeps 3:1 off the groove in both themes, with the single top-left light on its upper edge, so a level reads as a part of the unit, not a digital bar (R-005, apps/lab/progress pick B; A full ink rejected as too digital, C lit glass still heavy, D frosted glass under 3:1).

derivation.consequence: each hole is a recess (inverse light), never a printed dot
derivation.form: The groove is one long recess with elevation.well and surface.sunken, shade on its top-left inner edge.

derivation.consequence: no entry choreography, no idle animation; transitions only on state
derivation.form: The indeterminate form is a static row of printed ink ticks in the groove; nothing loops, sweeps or pulses.

derivation.consequence: a level change fills holes in reading order, ≤120ms, none under Reduce motion
derivation.form: A new value grows the fill from the start of the line in motion.fill; under reduce motion it jumps at once.

derivation.consequence: labels sit on the body's inset line, never floating mid-surface
derivation.form: The label is printed above the groove at the start, the reading at the end of the same line, never inside the fill.

derivation.consequence: tabular numerals, a 7-segment face for LCD values
derivation.form: The printed reading such as 38 min left or 64% uses tabular figures, so it keeps its width as it counts.

options.name: row of grille holes lighting in order
LCD bar segments in a window

variants.reason: A is one continuous recess that fills with ink (P4 colour and depth) and works for fine steps like 64%; B reads as a Grille level meter with a coarse 4% step, and C adds a second display window to a unit, which P2 keeps to one.

root.why: The label line and the groove stack at fixed positions, so the unit does not reflow when the task starts or ends.

head.why: One printed line above the groove holds the name at the start and the reading at the end.

label.why: The task name is the caption size in regular weight, printed in ink like a label on the case.

value.why: The reading uses tabular numerals in secondary ink so minutes and percent keep their width while counting.

groove.why: One long recess takes the inverse light, with shade on its top-left inner edge, sunk into the body like a grille hole.

fill.why: The fill is full-step ink from the start of the line, the same as a lit hole, and never orange.

ticks.why: The indeterminate pattern spreads its ticks along the groove and holds them still, because nothing moves while idle.

tick.why: Each tick is a short capsule of full-step ink in the groove, so working reads as ink, not as a colour.

sm.why: The small groove is 4px tall for lists of many devices where each row needs less height.

md.why: The default groove is 8px tall, the same as the fader track, the main reading of a unit.

@media prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.why: Under reduce motion the fill jumps to the new value at once, with no growth along the groove.

@media forced-colors: active.why: In forced colours the groove gets a real edge and the fill and ticks use the text colour, so the level survives.

inline-size.why: The fill grows along the reading direction in the fill time when the device reports a new value.
